csiro.lib
Class FFT

java.lang.Object
  |
  +--csiro.lib.FFT
public class FFT
extends java.lang.Object

Basic class of static public function for performing FFT's using exactly the notation of Numerical Recipes in C, Chs. 12 & 13 (Press et al), henceforth denoted NR. The calls for four1(), realft(), twofft() and convlv() are reproduced here. They are overloaded so as to work with common double[] arrays, but also the DoubleMatrix1D arrays from the cern.colt.matrix class libraries. Note that NR's unit--offset convention is used throughout, so most data vectors use elements data[1..n], where n=data.size()-1 if data is of type DoubleMatrix1D. The element data[0] is generally unused.

1.0, 9/8/2001

main

public static void main(java.lang.String[] args)
Simple test functions to convolve ascii stdin data with smoother via FFT

four1

public static void four1(cern.colt.matrix.DoubleMatrix1D data,
                         int nn,
                         int isign)
Replaces data[1..2*nn] by its DFT, if isign=1, otherwise replaces data[1..2*nn] by nn times its inverse DFT, if isign=-1.
data[1..2*nn] is a complex array of length nn. nn MUST be a power of 2.
N.B. data.size() = 2*nn+1, since by sticking to the NR unit-offset convention, we don't use element data[0]

twofft

public static void twofft(cern.colt.matrix.DoubleMatrix1D data1,
                          cern.colt.matrix.DoubleMatrix1D data2,
                          cern.colt.matrix.DoubleMatrix1D fft1,
                          cern.colt.matrix.DoubleMatrix1D fft2,
                          int n)
Given data1[1..nn] and data2[1..n], this calls four1 and returns two complex output arrays fft1[1..2n] and fft2[1..2n], which contain the DFT of the respective data arrays.
n MUST be a power of 2.
N.B. data1.size() = data2.size() = n+1 and fft1.size() = fft2.size() = 2n+1, since by sticking to the NR unit-offset convention, we don't use element data[0]

realft

public static void realft(cern.colt.matrix.DoubleMatrix1D data,
                          int n,
                          int isign)
Computes the DFT of a set of real data in data1[1..n], going forwards or backwards according to isign=1 or -1 respectively. the inverse transform must be multiplied by 2/n.
n MUST be a power of 2.
N.B. data.size() = n+1 and we don't use data[0].
See NR section 12.3 for all the gory detail.

convlv_clean

public static void convlv_clean(double[] data,
                                int n,
                                double[] respns,
                                int isign,
                                double[] ans)
Convolves data[1..n] with the response function respns[1..n]
n MUST be a power of 2.
This is the same as convlv(), but leaves the response function intact.
The response must be stored in respns[1..n] in wrap-around order, with user-supplied zero padding in the middle. N.B. We don't use data[0].
See NR section 13.1 for all the gory detail.
